    {
      "paper_id": "doi-10-3233-aic-2012-0516",
      "title": "Detection of imperative and declarative question–answer pairs in email conversations",
      "research_question": "Can email questions expressed in interrogative, imperative, declarative, and other forms be detected and paired with their answers more accurately than with approaches restricted mainly to interrogative questions and local paragraph structure?",
      "methodology": "The authors developed question-detection and question–answer pairing methods using lexical, contextual, and email-thread structural features and evaluated them on email from the Enron and CSpace corpora. A manually labeled 700-sentence set containing 350 questions and 350 non-questions was used for question detection, while separate human annotation was collected for question–answer pairing. Pairing systems included prior baselines and several heuristic and logistic-regression variants, evaluated with cross-validation and both strict and longest-common-subsequence-based matching metrics. The experiments also varied how many questions a candidate answer could be linked to.",
      "key_findings": [
        {
          "finding": "Non-interrogative formulations form a substantial minority of email questions; the authors' Enron sampling suggested roughly one fifth of questions were not conventional interrogatives.",
          "evidence_type": "supported",
          "section": "1, 4.2"
        },
        {
          "finding": "The proposed regular-expression question detector achieved approximately 0.907 F1 on the balanced evaluation set and handled imperative and declarative forms as well as interrogatives.",
          "evidence_type": "supported",
          "section": "4.2"
        },
        {
          "finding": "The authors' heuristic question–answer pairing variants generally improved over the tested naive and Shrestha-and-McKeown-style pairing baselines, although performance varied between annotator-derived evaluation sets.",
          "evidence_type": "supported",
          "section": "4.3"
        },
        {
          "finding": "Allowing an answer to be associated with more than one preceding question improved pairing performance modestly, and allowing up to three questions per answer produced the best result in the reported parameter experiment.",
          "evidence_type": "supported",
          "section": "4.3"
        },
        {
          "finding": "Human annotators showed substantial but imperfect agreement on both question segmentation and answer pairing, demonstrating that reply-to-question alignment is not fully deterministic even for human readers.",
          "evidence_type": "supported",
          "section": "4.3"
        },
        {
          "finding": "The implemented answer extractor operated at sentence granularity, while annotators sometimes selected larger spans, leaving multi-sentence and partially answering responses inadequately represented.",
          "evidence_type": "supported",
          "section": "4.3, 5"
        }
      ],
      "limitations": [
        "The task-specific question–answer annotations were created for the study because the authors found no adequate publicly annotated email corpus, and the paper does not state that these annotations were released.",
        "Question–answer extraction is primarily sentence based and does not model the internal propositions of a multi-sentence answer.",
        "The evaluation does not explicitly label whether a response fully answers, partially answers, or leaves individual components of a question unanswered.",
        "Although one answer can be linked to several questions, the model does not explicitly represent proposition-level many-to-many alignment.",
        "Annotation boundaries differed between annotators, particularly for answer extent.",
        "The experiments use English email corpora and may not generalize to other communication genres or languages."
      ],
      "reproducibility": {
        "code_available": false,
        "dataset_available": false,
        "metrics_reported": true
      },

        "one_answer_multiple_questions": 0.99,
        "human_alignment_variability": 0.96,
        "sentence_level_answer_limit": 0.97
      },
      "raw_claims": [
        "The task consists of detecting explicit and implicit questions in email and pairing them with answers when answers exist.",
        "Email questions are not restricted to sentences ending in question marks.",
        "The annotated question-detection sample contained interrogative, imperative, declarative, and other question forms.",
        "The proposed question detector obtained higher F1 than the tested simpler baselines on the balanced evaluation set.",
        "Question–answer pairing was annotated independently by multiple human annotators.",
        "Agreement on answer pairing was substantial but not perfect.",
        "The pairing model can permit a single answer to correspond to several questions.",
        "A maximum of three questions per answer gave the best result in the reported parameter experiment.",
        "Annotators could identify answer spans longer than the single-sentence units returned by the implemented extractor.",
        "The authors identify improved treatment of multi-sentence answers as future work."
      ],
      "source_url": "https://starlab.ewi.tudelft.nl/papers/n99.pdf",
      "access": "full_text"
    },

      "paper_id": "manual-be69c3aa17",
      "title": "Annotating Abstract Pronominal Anaphora in the DAD Project",
      "research_question": "Can an extension of the MATE/GNOME annotation scheme reliably capture abstract pronominal anaphora whose antecedents are verbal phrases, clauses, propositions, or larger discourse segments in Danish and Italian texts and dialogues?",
      "methodology": "The authors define the DAD annotation scheme for third-person singular pronouns that may refer to abstract discourse objects and apply it to Danish and Italian spoken and written corpora. The scheme distinguishes pronominal functions and records both antecedent spans and semantic types such as eventualities, facts, propositions, questions, and speech acts. Subsets of the material were independently annotated by two annotators, and intercoder agreement was measured with kappa for pronoun classification, antecedent identification, and referent attributes. The authors separately discuss cases where annotators selected antecedent spans that overlapped only partially.",
      "key_findings": [
        {
          "finding": "Annotators could identify abstract anaphora and their non-NP antecedents with generally substantial agreement in both Danish and Italian material.",
          "evidence_type": "supported",
          "section": "4"
        },
        {
          "finding": "Agreement for identifying non-NP antecedent segments was approximately in the high 0.7s to high 0.8s across the reported language and genre subsets.",
          "evidence_type": "supported",
          "section": "4"
        },
        {
          "finding": "Agreement on proposition-type abstract referents was high, with reported kappa values around 0.80 to 0.92 across the evaluated subsets.",
          "evidence_type": "supported",
          "section": "4"
        },
        {
          "finding": "Standard kappa treats two partially overlapping antecedent spans as a complete disagreement, even when the annotators substantially agree on the discourse material being referred to.",
          "evidence_type": "supported",
          "section": "4"
        },
        {
          "finding": "The authors explicitly identify partial-overlap scoring as an unresolved evaluation issue and suggest that an agreement measure sensitive to degrees of overlap would be preferable.",
          "evidence_type": "supported",
          "section": "4, 5"
        },
        {
          "finding": "Preliminary corpus comparisons indicate language- and genre-dependent differences in which syntactic constituents and abstract-object types are selected as antecedents.",
          "evidence_type": "supported",
          "section": "3, 5"
        }
      ],
      "limitations": [
        "Only subsets of the corpora were independently double annotated, and Italian double annotation was more limited than Danish double annotation.",
        "The annotators were experienced with the scheme, so agreement may overestimate performance achievable by less specialized annotators.",
        "The standard kappa calculation cannot distinguish a near-identical antecedent span from a completely different antecedent when spans merely overlap partially.",
        "The project was still constructing an agreed corpus, and the paper does not provide a released annotation package or reproducibility link.",
        "The study concerns abstract anaphora rather than question–reply alignment directly.",
        "The empirical coverage is limited to Danish and Italian datasets and the particular dialogue and text genres selected."

        "code_available": false,

        "metrics_reported": true

        "The DAD scheme extends an existing anaphora scheme to pronouns with verbal, clausal, and discourse-segment antecedents.",
        "The annotation distinguishes several kinds of abstract referents rather than treating all non-nominal antecedents alike.",
        "The annotated material contains both dialogue and written text in Danish and Italian.",
        "Independent annotation was used on selected portions of both languages to estimate reliability.",
        "Agreement values for the principal annotation categories were generally above 0.7.",
        "Annotators sometimes chose antecedent spans that overlapped without having identical boundaries.",
        "The reported kappa procedure counts partially overlapping spans as disagreement.",
        "The authors regard a more graded treatment of antecedent overlap as desirable.",
        "Propositions, eventualities, facts, questions, and speech acts are among the abstract referent categories represented in the scheme.",
        "The study reports preliminary differences in abstract-anaphora behavior across language and genre."
      ],
      "source_url": "https://www.researchgate.net/publication/220746223_Annotating_Abstract_Pronominal_Anaphora_in_the_DAD_Project",
      "access": "full_text"

    {
      "paper_id": "doi-10-18653-v1-2023-eacl-main-247",
      "title": "A simple but effective model for attachment in discourse parsing with multi-task learning for relation labeling",
      "research_question": "Can a relatively simple pairwise BERT discourse parser achieve competitive attachment and relation-labeling performance on multiparty dialogue while permitting discourse structures in which a single utterance attaches to multiple antecedents?",
      "methodology": "The authors train BERTLine on variants of the STAC multiparty-dialogue corpus, encoding pairs of elementary discourse units and augmenting their representations with structural information such as speaker change and distance. A linear binary classifier predicts attachments to preceding units within a fixed local window, allowing more than one predicted parent, while a multi-task architecture jointly learns attachment and one of 16 SDRT relation labels. They also construct a modified STAC-Squished corpus that collapses chains of adjacent nonlinguistic event units. Performance is evaluated with micro-averaged attachment and relation F1 and compared with previously reported discourse parsers.",
      "key_findings": [
        {
          "finding": "BERTLine achieved an attachment F1 of 73.06 and relation F1 of 56.25 on the standard STAC setting reported by the authors.",
          "evidence_type": "supported",
          "section": "4"
        },
        {
          "finding": "Joint attachment and relation learning improved relation labeling relative to a pipeline treatment while preserving competitive attachment performance.",
          "evidence_type": "supported",
          "section": "3, 4"
        },
        {
          "finding": "The model explicitly permits one discourse unit to have multiple parents instead of forcing a tree structure, which is important for utterances that simultaneously respond to or acknowledge several prior contributions.",
          "evidence_type": "supported",
          "section": "2, 3"
        },
        {
          "finding": "The test data contained 77 multi-parent structures, including eight structures with more than three parents, and the model recovered only about 20 percent of the multi-parent cases.",
          "evidence_type": "supported",
          "section": "4"
        },
        {
          "finding": "On the authors' squished STAC variant, performance increased substantially relative to the standard STAC configuration, including attachment F1 close to 80.",
          "evidence_type": "supported",
          "section": "4"
        },
        {
          "finding": "Question–Answer-Pair is included among the discourse relation labels, but the paper reports aggregate relation scores rather than separate empirical results for Question–Answer-Pair links, unanswered questions, or partial answers.",
          "evidence_type": "supported",
          "section": "2, 4"
        }
      ],
      "limitations": [
        "Multi-parent structures are comparatively rare in STAC, and the model captures only a minority of them.",
        "The ten-EDU attachment window prevents links to more distant antecedents.",
        "Reported relation metrics aggregate the 16 relation labels, so the paper does not provide a dedicated evaluation of Question–Answer-Pair alignment.",
        "The discourse representation does not explicitly label whether one antecedent proposition is fully or only partially addressed.",
        "The authors note the scarcity of diverse expert-annotated multiparty and situated dialogue corpora.",
        "Generalization to spoken conversation and other dialogue domains is not established.",
        "The authors identify further error analysis and evaluation on additional corpora as future work."
      ],
      "reproducibility": {
        "code_available": true,
        "dataset_available": true,
        "metrics_reported": true
      },
      "confidence_scores": {
        "standard_stac_performance": 0.99,
        "multitask_relation_gain": 0.97,

        "multi_parent_recall_low": 0.99,
        "squished_stac_gain": 0.98,
        "no_qap_specific_breakdown": 0.96
      },
      "raw_claims": [
        "BERTLine predicts discourse links by classifying pairs of discourse units.",
        "The attachment classifier considers preceding units within a bounded local window.",
        "A discourse unit can receive more than one predicted parent.",
        "The STAC relation inventory includes a Question–Answer-Pair relation.",
        "The multi-task model learns attachment and relation-label information together.",
        "The standard STAC result reported for BERTLine is 73.06 F1 for attachment and 56.25 F1 for relations.",
        "Multi-parent configurations occur in the STAC test data but are relatively infrequent.",
        "Only about one fifth of the observed multi-parent structures were recovered by the model.",
        "The authors collapse adjacent event-only sequences to construct the S-Squished corpus.",
        "Code associated with the paper and data are available from the LineBert repository."
      ],
      "source_url": "https://aclanthology.org/2023.eacl-main.247.pdf",
      "access": "full_text"
    },
    {
      "paper_id": "manual-7743c50805",
      "title": "Identifying reference to abstract objects in dialogue",
      "research_question": "Can human annotators reliably identify unconstrained stretches of prior dialogue that function as antecedents for discourse-deictic expressions, including antecedents spanning several utterances?",
      "methodology": "The authors conducted two annotation experiments on TRAINS-91 task-oriented dialogues in which annotators marked discourse-deictic antecedents as unconstrained regions of preceding text rather than selecting from predetermined syntactic units. In the first experiment, 19 completed annotations were obtained from initially recruited undergraduate annotators, and agreement was analyzed using set-based variants of Krippendorff's alpha as well as separate measures for antecedent beginnings and endings. A second, smaller experiment modified the annotation procedure after difficulties observed in the first. The analyses also compare pronoun types and inspect examples where different annotators chose partly overlapping or multi-utterance regions.",
      "key_findings": [
        {
          "finding": "Annotators showed meaningful convergence on the discourse regions serving as antecedents, although a simple distance-based model accounted for a substantial part of their behavior.",
          "evidence_type": "supported",
          "section": "3, 5"
        },
        {
          "finding": "For 16 readily identifiable anaphors in the first experiment, set-based agreement was moderate, with reported alpha values of approximately 0.45 under Jaccard overlap and 0.55 under Dice and Passonneau-style overlap.",
          "evidence_type": "supported",
          "section": "3"
        },
        {
          "finding": "Annotators agreed more strongly about where antecedent regions ended than about where they began, indicating uncertainty about how much preceding discourse belongs to a discourse-deictic antecedent.",
          "evidence_type": "supported",
          "section": "3"
        },
        {
          "finding": "Some discourse-deictic pronouns referred to material spanning several preceding utterances, and annotators could disagree between a narrow single-utterance antecedent and a broader multi-utterance antecedent.",
          "evidence_type": "supported",
          "section": "3, 5"
        },
        {
          "finding": "Demonstrative pronouns, especially forms such as 'that', were considerably more likely than ordinary 'it' or definite descriptions to receive discourse-segment antecedents.",
          "evidence_type": "supported",
          "section": "3, 4, 5"
        },
        {
          "finding": "Approximately one fifth of the markables in each experiment were judged to have plausible discourse-segment antecedents after the authors' filtering and interpretation of the annotations.",
          "evidence_type": "supported",
          "section": "5"
        }
      ],
      "limitations": [
        "Only a small number of TRAINS-91 dialogues were used, so the empirical sample is narrow.",
        "The domain is collaborative route or plan construction, which may create unusually many references to plans and previously discussed actions.",
        "Annotators were overhearers rather than participants in the original conversations and therefore lacked the participants' grounding state.",
        "The second experiment produced too few usable observations for a meaningful numerical agreement analysis.",
        "A simple distance model explained a considerable amount of the annotation behavior, weakening interpretations of raw boundary agreement.",
        "The annotation representation was not always sensitive enough to distinguish subtle semantic differences between a proposition, an elaboration of it, and a larger complex discourse object.",
        "The paper studies discourse deixis rather than explicit question–reply completeness."
      ],
      "reproducibility": {
        "code_available": false,
        "dataset_available": false,
        "metrics_reported": true
      },
      "confidence_scores": {
        "annotator_convergence": 0.96,
        "set_based_agreement": 0.98,
        "end_boundaries_easier": 0.96,
        "multi_utterance_antecedents": 0.99,
        "demonstratives_prefer_discourse_antecedents": 0.98,
        "segment_reference_frequency": 0.96
      },
      "raw_claims": [
        "Annotators were allowed to mark arbitrary stretches of prior dialogue as antecedents.",
        "The first experiment used a TRAINS-91 dialogue and many independently working annotators.",
        "Thirty-five of 181 markables in the first experiment received a segment antecedent from at least three annotators.",
        "Set-overlap agreement for the clearest cases was moderate rather than perfect.",
        "Antecedent ending boundaries were more consistently identified than antecedent beginnings.",
        "Some disagreements involved two annotations that shared discourse material but differed in how much preceding context they included.",
        "A pronoun can refer to an abstract object evoked by several prior utterances rather than by one syntactic constituent.",
        "Demonstrative pronouns were the strongest source of clearly identified discourse-deictic references.",
        "The second experiment again produced a proportion of plausible discourse-segment references close to one fifth of the analyzed markables.",
        "The authors argue that discourse deixis is common enough to require explicit treatment in dialogue models."
      ],
      "source_url": "https://www.semdial.org/anthology/semdial2006_brandial_proceedings.pdf",
      "access": "full_text"
    },
    {
      "paper_id": "doi-10-18653-v1-s15-1035",
      "title": "Resolving Discourse-Deictic Pronouns: A Two-Stage Approach to Do It",
      "research_question": "Can discourse-deictic instances of 'it', 'this', and 'that' be automatically distinguished from nominal uses and then resolved to verbal or clausal antecedents accurately enough to improve general coreference resolution?",
      "methodology": "The authors use the English CoNLL-2012/OntoNotes data and implement two maximum-entropy stages: one classifies a pronoun as discourse deictic and the second selects a verbal antecedent. Candidate antecedents are verbs in the pronoun's sentence and the three preceding sentences, following the OntoNotes convention of representing a clausal antecedent through a verbal head. Feature and decision thresholds are tuned on development data, and the stages are evaluated both separately and when integrated with two existing coreference systems. The authors additionally conduct a manual error analysis that distinguishes model errors from questionable or incomplete gold annotations.",
      "key_findings": [
        {
          "finding": "The two-stage model outperformed the tested baselines for both discourse-deictic classification and antecedent resolution.",
          "evidence_type": "supported",
          "section": "5"
        },
        {
          "finding": "For discourse-deixis classification, the two-stage system achieved 35.2 precision, 42.9 recall, and 38.6 F1 overall in the reported experiment.",
          "evidence_type": "supported",
          "section": "5"
        },
        {
          "finding": "With oracle knowledge that a pronoun was discourse deictic, antecedent resolution reached 55.7 precision, 42.5 recall, and 48.2 F1; with system classification, end-to-end antecedent resolution fell to 22.2 F1.",
          "evidence_type": "supported",
          "section": "5"
        },
        {
          "finding": "Adding discourse-deixis handling to two general coreference systems produced small improvements in aggregate CoNLL score, with most reported differences statistically significant despite their small magnitude.",
          "evidence_type": "supported",
          "section": "5"
        },
        {
          "finding": "The manual error analysis categorized 20 percent of the examined apparent errors as multiple-antecedent cases and identified additional cases in which the gold annotation was missing or only partially represented an acceptable antecedent.",
          "evidence_type": "supported",
          "section": "6"
        },
        {
          "finding": "The authors conclude from cases with overlapping, elaborated, or multiple plausible antecedents that strict evaluation against one gold verbal antecedent can penalize semantically reasonable resolutions and that a more flexible evaluation is needed.",
          "evidence_type": "supported",
          "section": "6, 7"
        }
      ],
      "limitations": [
        "OntoNotes represents clausal antecedents using a single verbal head, which can collapse a multi-proposition discourse referent into one token-level target.",
        "The error analysis shows that some gold annotations omit plausible antecedents or encode only part of a larger discourse antecedent.",
        "The evaluation generally assumes a unique gold antecedent even though multiple antecedents may be semantically acceptable.",
        "The system is restricted to the pronouns 'it', 'this', and 'that'.",
        "Antecedent candidates are limited to the current and previous three sentences.",
        "The two stages do not jointly model competition between nominal and discourse-deictic antecedents.",
        "The feature-based model uses mostly local linguistic information and only limited broader discourse structure.",
        "The test data are strongly imbalanced, particularly because most occurrences of 'it' are not discourse deictic."
      ],
      "reproducibility": {
        "code_available": false,
        "dataset_available": true,
        "metrics_reported": true
      },
      "confidence_scores": {
        "two_stage_beats_baselines": 0.99,
        "classification_metrics": 0.99,
        "resolution_metrics": 0.99,
        "coreference_system_gain": 0.98,
        "multiple_antecedent_errors": 0.99,
        "strict_gold_evaluation_problem": 0.99
      },
      "raw_claims": [
        "Discourse-deictic pronouns have verbal or clausal rather than nominal antecedents.",
        "The system first determines whether a pronoun is discourse deictic and then resolves its antecedent.",
        "The experiments focus on the pronouns 'it', 'this', and 'that'.",
        "The CoNLL-2012 test material contains 2075 candidate pronouns, of which 252 are annotated as discourse deictic.",
        "Candidate verbal antecedents are drawn from the current sentence and the preceding three sentences.",
        "The two-stage system outperforms the comparison systems on the dedicated discourse-deixis experiments.",
        "Errors in detecting discourse deixis propagate to the subsequent antecedent-resolution stage.",
        "Adding discourse deixis yields small improvements to two complete coreference resolvers.",
        "Manual inspection found cases where more than one antecedent was linguistically acceptable.",
        "Some apparent system errors resulted from missing or partial gold annotation rather than an obviously incorrect system choice.",
        "The authors argue that discourse-deixis evaluation should permit more flexible matching of antecedents."
      ],
      "source_url": "https://aclanthology.org/S15-1035.pdf",
      "access": "full_text"
    }
  ],
  "skipped": []
}
